title: Menu items that are settings wear a checkmark instead of rewording themselves
goal: Show Grid changes its wording to Hide Grid when the grid is on, and Snap to Grid becomes Stop Snapping to Grid. That is how an action is written, not a setting. Something that is simply on or off should keep one name and carry a checkmark when it is on, so you can see the state without reading a sentence, and so the item does not move under the pointer as its label changes length.
notes: Asked for by the user on 2026-09-05 about Show Grid. No menu item in the app uses a checkmark today: EditorCommands.swift flips the title of every stateful item instead, at line 527 for the grid, 536 for snapping, 492 for the layers panel and 503 for the Library, and MainMenuTitles.swift retitles the history item the same way. The Mac convention is a checkmark for something that is on or off and a changing verb only for an action, so the panel and Library items are worth judging individually rather than converting blindly: hiding a panel reads as an action to some people. Show and Hide History is the one to be most careful with, since it is retitled from a separate file and is reached from the menu bar agent as well as the editor, and there is an open task about those two disagreeing with each other; check it before touching that one. SwiftUI menu items take a Toggle for exactly this, which also gives the right accessibility state, rather than drawing a tick by hand.
acceptance: Show Grid keeps that name at all times and carries a checkmark while the grid is showing
Snap to Grid does the same, and the other settings of this kind in the menus follow the same rule
Items that genuinely perform an action, rather than hold a state, keep their changing wording, and the audit says which items were judged to be which and why
Every one of these still works from its keyboard shortcut, and the shortcut is shown once rather than moving between two items
Nothing changes about what any of them does
Audit written under queue/audits/ with the View menu open in both states, anything rough filed as a follow-up
